maria: Heads-up — noticed a sudden drop in priming cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout (affinity tweak + mixed quant path).
jia: How big is the delta? any graphs?
maria: Seeded prompts hit-rate fell from ~91% -> ~62% for pool-3 p99 path. Token output per request increased ~28%. Quick perf snippet below.
```
bench-bot: perf snapshot @3498660000: pool-3 kernel-select-v2 applied
  priming_hit_rate: 0.62 (was 0.91)
  tokens_per_request: 187 -> 239
  p50_latency_ms: 12 -> 15
  p99_latency_ms: 98 -> 126
  batch_window_ms: 4.8 -> 7.2
```
bench-bot: also saw KV cache warmup slope flattening (longer to reach steady hit rate).
sam: Any chance the cache keys changed? canonicalization? normalization?
maria: Yes — runtime team changed key fingerprinting in kernel-select-v2: old key = sha1(prefix + len + norm_flags), new key = xxhash64(prefix + session_id) for scheduler affinity. We missed re-applying tokenizer normalization step into the hash.
leah: That switch was to reduce cross-shard collisions for the new scheduler. We didn't expect tokenizer normalization to be required for priming since we assumed stable prefixes. My bad, missed a callout. cc @devon
devon: I reproduced locally: when I reintroduce normalization into key generation the hit-rate recovers to ~88% on same sample workload. Quick diff:
```
- key = xxhash64(prefix + session)
+ key = xxhash64(normalize(prefix) + session)
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-select-v2 rolled to pool-3 @3498650000. Current state: degraded. Recommendations?
sam: Before full rollback, can we try a compatibility shim that maps old-key -> new-key for hot prefixes? An alias table in front of KV cache could warm things without reverting kernel.
leah: I can spin up an alias table in memcache and backfill top-500 prefixes. That should give immediate improvement for high-frequency flows.
bench-bot: additional profiling: batching heuristics altered by affinity shift (requests now routed less evenly -> smaller batch assembly per worker). Observed: average batch size down 12%, batch latency variance up.
maria: Plan: 1) hotfix to restore tokenizer-normalization in key gen (patch by devon), 2) alias mapping for top prefixes for 24h warmup, 3) canary kernel-select-v2 with normalization enabled, 4) rollback if < +15% hit-rate improvement in 2h. I'll open the PR and the incident runbook.
devon: PR created: https://github.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4123 — includes tests for key stability and a small perf guard. Also adding an additional check: mixed-quant codepath sometimes chooses a different kernel variant which shifted KV offset calculation in one model family; added a unit test to validate kv-offset invariant across kernel variants.
leah: Nice. I'll coordinate warmup and backfill scripts (will push list of top prefixes to #eng-runtime once ready).
maria: Good catch everyone. Post-mortem TODOs: make key-gen contract explicit (normalization MUST be part of key), add canary that runs hit-rate smoke for priming before kernel rollouts, and add a regression alert on priming hit-rate drop >10% within 1h of deploy.
sam: Agreed — and we should include a fallback routing policy that sends priming-heavy routes to the pre-rollout kernel variant during transitions.
bench-bot: after aliasing + normalization patch on a small canary: priming_hit_rate -> 89% within 30m, p99_latency back to ~102ms. Will monitor.
maria: Closing loop: schedule a coordinated rollout window and update the kernel selection checklist with key-gen contract. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
